# Smoosh — Product Requirements Document

**Version:** 1.0  
**Date:** 2026-09-27  
**Author:** Generated by Claude  
**Status:** Draft

> Game rules, tier numbers, and shader details live in `smoosh-GAME_DESIGN_MERGE_TIERS.md`. Visual style, storyline, and Higgsfield art direction live in `smoosh-ART_AND_STORY_DIRECTION.md`. This PRD references those docs rather than repeating their content.

> ⚠️ Assumption: "Smoosh" is a working title; a shortlist (Fuse, Meld, Kindred, Fusepop, and 20+ others) has been generated but not finalized. Repo: `github.com/spencertownley-sys/Merge_Game1`.

> **Revised 2026-09-28 (first pass):** the initial build is scoped to the core merge game and the "Scattered Skylight" story/journey first, with a pastel-watercolor-anime visual style. Photo personalization (Fusion/Ladder skins) is built as a distinct second stage, after the core game — not because it needs to be paid, but because getting the core loop right first is the priority.
>
> **Revised 2026-09-28 (second pass):** the photo-personalization stage is **free**, not a paid add-on. Its risk profile turned out to hinge on two separable things: (a) whether content is ever shared/hosted/visible to anyone but the uploader, and (b) how strongly age is verified. Keeping the feature **strictly private and on-device — never uploaded, never included in the share card, never synced — removes essentially all of the sharing-related risk** (UGC moderation duty, App Store UGC guidelines, cross-user consent, any CSAM-hosting obligation), independent of payment. Age assurance is handled the original way: an **18+ self-attestation** screen the first time the feature is opened. This is knowingly a weaker age-assurance mechanism than a purchase gate, but paired with the private/non-public design, the consequences of a wrong self-attestation are much smaller than they were in the original all-in design — nothing produced by the feature is ever seen by anyone but its creator. See §7 for the full reasoning.

---

## 1. Overview

### 1.1 Problem Statement

Physics-merge games (Suika Game and its many clones) are compulsively playable, but every clone is the same game with a different set of fruits. Players have no personal connection to what they are merging, and no reason to send a run to a friend beyond a raw score.

### 1.2 Proposed Solution

Smoosh is a physics merge game set in a fully fictional, pastel-watercolor-anime fantasy world: a Skylight shattered into scattered motes, and the player travels from a peaceful starting village through increasingly fantastical lands, merging motes back into brighter and brighter orbs to restore each land's color and light. A journey map gives the run-to-run structure. The tier orbs themselves render as glossy, translucent gummy-candy spheres — round while falling, squashing playfully on landing — that turn to look at your finger. As a second build stage, players can unlock **Fusion and Ladder skins** (free, 18+ self-attested, strictly private) — putting their own (or friends') faces on the balls, with Fusion blending two faces together on merge — rendered as a face glowing inside that same translucent gummy material, rather than printed on its surface. The personalization stays entirely on-device and is never shared, uploaded, or included in the (otherwise shareable) end-of-run card.

### 1.3 Goals

- **Primary goal:** Make the merge loop and the land-by-land story feel great as a standalone experience — no personalization feature should be required to enjoy the core game.
- **Secondary goals:**
  - A journey/story structure that gives players a reason to come back tomorrow.
  - A shareable end-of-run artifact that markets the game.
  - A web-first build that ports to iOS and Android with minimal rewrite.
  - A personal hook (photo fusion) that differentiates from other merge games, built as a second stage once the core game is solid, kept low-risk by staying strictly private/on-device rather than by charging for it.

### 1.4 Non-Goals

- Cloning any existing game's art, name, or audio.
- Real-time (live) multiplayer.
- Photorealistic deepfake-quality face morphing. The fusion is stylized and playful.
- Photo personalization in the _very first_ build pass — it's built as a second stage after the core game, not simultaneously, but it is not paid or otherwise gated beyond the 18+ self-attestation.
- Sharing, cloud sync, or including personalized photos in any output visible to anyone but the uploader — this stays permanently out of scope for the personalization feature itself (distinct from Phase 3's _unrelated_ async-challenge sharing, which never involves photos).
- Ads and in-app purchases in the initial MVP (see §7 for the monetization surfaces planned later).
- 3D camera movement or a 3D physics engine.

## 2. Target Users

### 2.1 Primary User Persona

| Field      | Detail                                                                                            |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Who        | Casual mobile gamer, 22–45, plays in short bursts (commute, waiting, alongside a podcast or show) |
| Pain       | Merge games get repetitive. Nothing about the game is _theirs_.                                   |
| Goal       | A satisfying few minutes of play; something fun to show friends                                   |
| Context    | Phone in one hand, sitting or standing, sound on or off, sessions of 3–10 minutes                 |
| Tech savvy | Low to medium                                                                                     |

### 2.2 Secondary Personas

| Persona                                          | Difference from primary                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Group organizer** (friend group, family, team) | Creates the skin set and gets everyone to play it. Cares about how easy it is to add photos and share.  |
| **Creator / streamer**                           | Uses their audience's or co-hosts' faces. Cares about the share card and a clean capture-friendly view. |
| **Pet / meme person**                            | Uses Ladder mode with pets, memes, or objects. No face detection needed.                                |

## 3. User Stories & Requirements

### 3.1 Core Play

**User story:** As a player, I want to drag and drop balls that merge when matching ones touch, so that I can chase a high score.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Dragging on the board moves the held ball along the drop rail; releasing drops it.
- [ ] A ghost guide line shows where the ball will fall.
- [ ] Same-tier balls merge on contact into the next tier per the tier table.
- [ ] The next ball is previewed.
- [ ] Score, best score, and combo are visible in the HUD.
- [ ] The run ends per the game-over rule and shows a results screen.
- [ ] Physics runs at a fixed timestep; a run with the same seed and same inputs produces the same result.
- [ ] 60 fps on a mid-range phone (2020-era) with a full board.

### 3.2 Photo Skins (Fusion & Ladder) — Free, Private, Second Build Stage

**User story:** As a player who's enjoyed the core game, I want to put my friends' faces on the balls and watch them fuse when they merge, so that the game becomes about us — without worrying about those photos going anywhere I don't control.

**Acceptance criteria (build this stage after the core game and story ship, not simultaneously):**

- [ ] Before I can open the skin editor for the first time, I confirm I am 18 or older; under that, the skin editor is not accessible and I only ever see default (non-photo) skins.
- [ ] The age-confirmation screen also states plainly, in one line, that this feature is fully private — photos and the faces they produce are never uploaded, synced, or shown to anyone else, including in the share card.
- [ ] I can create unlimited skin sets, name them, and add photos from camera roll or camera — no per-set photo limit.
- [ ] Each photo is auto-aligned and cropped on-device; I can adjust pan and zoom manually.
- [ ] I can preview my photo glowing inside the actual gummy ball before saving.
- [ ] In Fusion mode, merging two balls produces a ball whose face is a blend of both parents.
- [ ] In Ladder mode, I can assign one photo per tier (tiers 1-11) and the tier order is respected; with more than 11 photos in a Ladder set, the extras are available as alternates I can swap in per tier.
- [ ] If no face is detected, I am told and can still use the photo.
- [ ] Original photos, crops, and fused results never leave the device — no server upload, no analytics capture, no inclusion in crash reports, and excluded from OS-level app backups (iCloud/Google auto-backup) where the platform allows that exclusion.
- [ ] The share card (§3.4) never includes a personalized photo/face, even if the top ball in a run used one — it falls back to the equivalent default Skylight-mote art for that tier.
- [ ] I can delete a skin set and all its photos at any time.
- [ ] A "Simple graphics" option renders flat circles for low-end devices.

### 3.3 Journey Map

**User story:** As a player, I want a series of levels with goals, so that I always have a next thing to beat.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] A scrolling map shows levels, locked and unlocked states, and stars earned.
- [ ] A level intro shows the goal(s) and any constraints (drop limit, timer, obstacles).
- [ ] Completing a level awards 1–3 stars and unlocks the next level.
- [ ] Rock, ice, and wind mechanics work as specified.
- [ ] Progress persists across sessions (local storage in Phase 1).
- [ ] Journey levels can use a photo skin once the player has set one up (default Skylight-mote skins always work everywhere).

### 3.4 Share Card

**User story:** As a player, I want to share a card of my best run showing who merged into my top ball, so that friends see it and want to play.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] At game over, "Share" generates a 1080 × 1350 PNG.
- [ ] The card shows score, top ball, a small merge tree, and (in Fusion) a contribution bar of faces.
- [ ] Uses the native share sheet where available, otherwise downloads.
- [ ] No photo other than those already in the player's own skin set appears on the card.

### 3.5 Settings & Accessibility

**User story:** As a player, I want to control sound, haptics, motion, and graphics.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Toggles: sound, music, haptics (where supported), reduce motion, simple graphics, show tier numbers.
- [ ] Rim styles distinguish tiers without relying on color.
- [ ] Touch targets are at least 44 px.
- [ ] Game is playable one-handed in portrait.

### 3.6 Accounts, Daily Seed & Cloud Sync (Phase 2)

**User story:** As a player, I want to sign in so that my skins and progress follow me, and I can compete on a daily challenge.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Guest play continues to work with no account.
- [ ] Sign-in via email magic link, plus Apple and Google.
- [ ] Skin sets and progress sync across devices; guest data can be merged into a new account.
- [ ] Daily Seed shows today's seed, my best, and a leaderboard.
- [ ] Deleting my account removes all my data, including photos, within 30 days.

### 3.7 Social Sharing & Async Challenges (Phase 3)

**User story:** As a player, I want to send a friend the same drop sequence to see who scores higher, and invite them to use my skin set.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] I can create a challenge link that fixes the seed.
- [ ] A friend plays on their own time; results are compared after both finish.
- [ ] Sharing a skin set requires that the people pictured are the ones being invited or that I confirm I have permission; recipients can report and remove content.
- [ ] Content reporting and blocking exist for every user-generated photo that can be seen by another user.

> ⚠️ Note: cloud sync of skin sets/photos is intentionally **not** on this roadmap. The personalization feature's whole risk profile depends on staying strictly on-device; syncing it to any server would reopen the sharing/hosting risk category §7 was written to avoid. If cross-device sync of personalized skins is ever wanted, it needs its own risk review, not a default assumption that Phase 2 accounts extend to it — Phase 2 accounts cover progress/leaderboards only.

### Out of Scope

| Feature                                                                                   | Reason                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Live multiplayer                                                                          | Cost and complexity; async covers the social need                                                    |
| Ads and in-app purchases in the initial build                                             | Decide after retention data — see §7 for the planned later monetization mix                          |
| Copying another game's name, art, or audio                                                | Legal risk and no differentiation                                                                    |
| Uploading original (uncropped) photos, or any cloud sync/sharing of photos or fused faces | Privacy — the personalization feature is permanently on-device/private by design, not just at launch |

## 6. Assumptions & Risks

| #   | Assumption / Risk                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Impact                                                                                                                          | Mitigation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Face photos are sensitive personal data. Some jurisdictions regulate biometric identifiers (e.g., Illinois, Texas, Washington). Landmark detection may count as processing even when nothing leaves the device — this is a genuinely unsettled legal question, not a solved one. | High                                                                                                                            | Deferred to Phase 1.5, built after the core game. Process on-device only, never upload originals, crops, or fused results anywhere (no server, no analytics, no crash reports, excluded from OS-level app backups where the platform allows it). Explicit 18+ + "this stays private" screen before first use. Legal review before this stage ships. _This is not legal advice._ |
| 2   | Uploading friends' faces without their consent, even if the result is never shared with anyone else.                                                                                                                                                                             | Med                                                                                                                             | Consent micro-copy at the point of adding a photo, framed around the fact that nothing leaves the device — lower stakes than a sharing feature, but still worth stating plainly.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 3   | User-generated images can be abusive or illegal; platforms that host or transmit UGC have moderation/reporting obligations (including, in the US, CSAM reporting).                                                                                                               | Low (was High)                                                                                                                  | Materially reduced by design: nothing is ever hosted, transmitted, or shown to anyone but the person who made it, so there's no UGC being distributed. This protection only holds as long as the feature never gains a share/sync path — see the Phase 2/3 note in §4 keeping cloud sync and sharing off the roadmap for personalized content specifically.                     |
| 4   | Apple App Review Guideline 1.2 and Google Play UGC policy require filtering, reporting, and blocking for UGC visible to other users.                                                                                                                                             | Low (was High)                                                                                                                  | Likely doesn't apply as written, since content is never visible to anyone but its creator — but confirm this read with whoever does the legal review before submitting to either store, since store policy interpretation can be stricter than the letter of the rule.                                                                                                          |
| 5   | A free 18+ self-attestation is a weak age-assurance mechanism — a minor can simply tap through it.                                                                                                                                                                               | Med (was High under the free/shared design; downgraded here because the consequence of a wrong attestation is now much smaller) | Accepted trade-off: paired with the strictly private/on-device design, a wrong attestation exposes nothing beyond the device it happened on — no distribution, no hosting, no other person affected. App-wide minimum age stays 13+ regardless. Revisit this if the feature ever grows a sharing/sync path (it shouldn't, per §4's note).                                       |
| 6   | High-tier faces converge to a blurry average under naive blending.                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Med                                                                                                                             | F1 two-band blend; F2 morph; lineage-seeded detail preference.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 7   | Face detection fails on some photos (angles, occlusion, pets).                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Med                                                                                                                             | Manual pan/zoom fallback; Ladder mode for non-faces.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 8   | Physics feel is subjective and makes or breaks the game.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | High                                                                                                                            | Tuning panel from day one; playtest weekly; keep every constant in config.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 9   | Cross-browser physics divergence breaks seeded fairness.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Med                                                                                                                             | Deterministic Rapier build and fixed timestep; determinism tests in CI.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 10  | Fragment shader spheres are slow on old phones.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Med                                                                                                                             | "Simple graphics" fallback; texture pooling; perf budget in CI.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 11  | The genre is crowded; discovery is hard.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Med                                                                                                                             | Lead with the share card and face-fusion hook in all marketing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 12  | Similarity to existing games invites IP complaints.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Med                                                                                                                             | Original names, art, audio; genre mechanics are not the concern, assets are.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## 7. Decisions (resolved 2026-09-28)

- **Name:** working title still open; shortlist includes Fuse, Meld, Kindred, Fusepop, and 20+ others generated 2026-09-27. Final pick pending.
- **Domain/hosting:** a fresh domain, deployed from a new GitHub repository: `github.com/spencertownley-sys/Merge_Game1`.
- **Monetization:** rewarded/interstitial ads after a level loss, cosmetic IAP (premium default-skin packs — never affects gameplay), purchasable power-ups (gameplay-affecting — restricted to Classic mode only; Journey and any seeded/competitive mode stay power-up-free to preserve fairness), a one-time lifetime "Pro" unlock, and a monthly no-ads subscription. **Photo personalization is explicitly not a paid feature** — it's free, so it isn't part of the monetization plan.
- **Minimum age & photo features (revised 2026-09-28, second pass):** app-wide minimum age stays 13 (COPPA line), self-attested age gate on first launch. Photo/skin-creation (Phase 1.5, built after the core game, not simultaneously) is **free**, gated by its own **18+ self-attestation** the first time the skin editor is opened, paired with a plain statement that the feature is permanently private — nothing it produces is ever uploaded, synced, or shown to anyone but its creator, not even in the share card. That privacy design is what makes a self-attestation (rather than a purchase) an acceptable bar here — see risk #3-#5. ToS still prohibits uploading photos of minors regardless. This remains a conservative-but-imperfect policy pending actual legal review before this stage ships (see risk #1) — not legal advice.
- **Visual style (added 2026-09-28):** pastel watercolor anime, not glossy 3D-toy — see `ART_AND_STORY_DIRECTION.md`.
- **Journey structure (revised 2026-09-28):** fully fictional "lands" telling an original story ("The Scattered Skylight"), not tied to the podcast or any real travel content, starting from a low-stakes tutorial village. 13 lands at launch. Full list and per-land art direction in `ART_AND_STORY_DIRECTION.md` §4.
- **Business partner (photobooth venture):** unrelated; no cross-over.
- **Default art & audio:** the creator will commission these via Higgsfield using the prompts in `ART_AND_STORY_DIRECTION.md` §2-3.
- **Skin sets:** unlimited skin sets, unlimited photos per set — no free-tier cap, since there's no paid tier to differentiate from.
- **Hall of Faces gallery:** deferred to a later phase, not Phase 1.
